note: Where the two HTTP surfaces are hosted. Public URLs only — no credentials. Read by scripts/check-hosted.mjs, which tests them, and by scripts/check-docs.mjs, which refuses to let the README claim an address nothing tests.

web.serves: the read-only market page, staged by scripts/build-vercel.mjs from the same allowlist scripts/serve-web.mjs serves

play.serves: the play API the market page and the Minecraft plugin call
play.keys_held_note: The relayer (full-access, because a SignedDelegate is not a function call) plus one scoped key per pre-funded pool player, which is what scripts/build-render-secret.mjs ships. This field used to name a single legacy player that is not in the pool; nothing reads it, which is why it went stale.
play.keys_withheld: the root account, the items/market/guard contract accounts, every merchant and every agent

minecraft.how: Render cannot host a Minecraft server: it exposes HTTP only on 80/443, UDP is not on its roadmap, and its TCP support reaches only its own private network. So a joinable server runs on the maintainer's machine behind a tunnel (playit.gg or similar) and points the plugin at the hosted play service over https. Put the tunnel address here and `npm run check:hosted` will ping it with Minecraft's own Server List Ping and check the MOTD is this one. Empty means no server is advertised, and the check says so instead of passing.
minecraft.honest_limit: Live while that machine is on. A demo window, not hosting.
